parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
over means finished, as in 'the game is over'

explanation.surface: Someone reveals the record that has just been completed.
explanation.definitionFit: To uncover something hidden is to lay it bare, which is what exposing does.

clue.text: It's idle to have a smart party over a time of abstinence

indicators.note: in a down clue 'over' places the earlier pieces on top of the next

parts.note: in means fashionable or smart
a do is a party
Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: A lazy person throws a fashionable party just before Lent begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' in a down clue puts IN and DO above LENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Lazy people are slothful, avoiding effort, which is what idle means.

clue.text: It's universal feminine practice at the opera

definitions.text: It's universal feminine practice at the opera

parts.words: It's universal feminine practice at the opera
parts.note: the title of a Mozart opera translates as 'all women do thus', a habit common to every woman

explanation.surface: A remark that all women behave this way at the opera.
explanation.walkthrough: Mozart's comic opera's Italian title means 'so do all women', so the clue translates the title.
explanation.definitionFit: Mozart and Da Ponte's opera title says women all behave alike, a universal female practice.

parts.note: a fly-by-night is a shady dealer, but here creatures literally fly at night and bleed victims dry

explanation.surface: Shady racketeers who disappear overnight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly-by-night' means untrustworthy; here it is literal, creatures flying at night that suck blood, as extortioners bleed people.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloodsucking undead creatures in bat form fly at night, and swindlers who bleed people are given the same name.

clue.text: Arch in' high colours by E. London artist

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
Bow is a district of East London

explanation.surface: An East London painter depicts an arch in brilliant colours.
explanation.walkthrough: RA stands for Royal Academician; BOW is a district in the East End of London.
explanation.definitionFit: The coloured band across the sky after rain forms a curved span.

clue.text: I'm deep in trouble through hold-up

indicators.note: in trouble suggests the letters of the phrase before it are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in a traffic jam admits to being in deep trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' rearranges I'M DEEP.
explanation.definitionFit: To obstruct or delay progress is to hinder, the verb sense of hold up.

parts.note: a body part followed by love (O, the zero score) makes a word for a state of forgotten neglect

explanation.surface: A question whether some club member would welcome being forgotten.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is O in tennis scoring; add it to this body part and you get LIMBO, a state of neglect or oblivion.
explanation.definitionFit: An arm or leg is a member of the body, and adding O makes a word for forgotten neglect.

parts.note: an actor becomes word-perfect in a part by practising it

explanation.surface: Advice on achieving partial perfection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partly perfect' seems to mean half-good, but it is perfect in one's part, as an actor practising lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors practise lines before performance until word-perfect in their role.

clue.text: Lot's descendant is an old fossil

explanation.surface: A biblical lineage traced to a fossil, as if Lot's heir were very old.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis the Ammonites descend from Ben-Ammi, son of Lot; the same name belongs to the coiled shells found as fossils.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical tribe sprang from Lot's son, and the spiral-shelled extinct mollusc is a classic petrified remain.

parts.note: DD is Doctor of Divinity, the theologian's degree; with the 's it reads DD'S

explanation.surface: A churchman's arithmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: To sum figures is to total them, the verb sense of 'sums'.

clue.text: It's immaterial that I can muse inwardly

indicators.note: inwardly tells us the musing goes inside the phrase meaning 'I can'

parts.note: 'I can' is 'I am able', shortened to I'M ABLE
to muse is to ponder

explanation.surface: Someone declares their idle thoughts are of no consequence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I can' must be expanded to 'I am able', contracted, before 'inwardly' signals the musing going inside it; 'It's' and 'that' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Something weightless or intangible cannot be weighed, so it is without material substance.

parts.note: someone equally skilled with either hand has, in effect, a right hand on each side

explanation.surface: A question about a dispute where both parties are in the right.
explanation.walkthrough: It looks like a quarrel where both are justified; it is about hands, as if both were right hands.
explanation.definitionFit: A person able to use both hands equally well is as if right-handed on each side.

clue.text: How birds get in condition in spring

definitions.text: How birds get in condition in spring

parts.words: How birds get in condition in spring
parts.note: birds pair off again each spring, and putting something in good condition is to mend it; the word joins both readings

explanation.surface: A naturalist's note on how birds get fit in spring.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as RE-PAIR, birds coupling afresh in spring; read whole, it is to mend, putting something back in condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Mending restores a thing to good order, and birds forming couples again each breeding season do so anew.

parts.note: major means superior or senior, put over others
Ursa is Latin for bear

explanation.surface: A star-gazer's question about the Great Bear constellation.
explanation.walkthrough: Ursa Major is the Great Bear; read in parts it is a bear placed over others, which is what domineering does.
explanation.definitionFit: To dominate is to override or browbeat others, which is the sense of this verb.

clue.text: He figures as a politician, sometimes

explanation.surface: A man who crunches numbers and is occasionally in government.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is an old name for a statistician, a man of figures, and also for a politician or advocate of state control.
explanation.definitionFit: A numbers man dealing in statistics once had this name, and so did a statesman or believer in state power.

clue.text: Get the car away in, one piece for the tea party.

annotationWithheld.why: Get the car away in one piece for the tea party (4,4): no parse found; nothing in 'Get the car away in one' builds SEED, and a search of the clue gave nothing
annotationWithheld.clue: Get the car away in, one piece for the tea party.

clue.text: Article Edison altered to, coat metal

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: altered says the letters of the inventor's name are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: Something written by the inventor Edison is revised to explain how to plate metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'altered' shuffles the inventor's name, which follows the article; the comma after 'to' is a misprint on the page.
explanation.definitionFit: Anodising coats aluminium or another metal with a protective oxide layer by electrolysis.

parts.note: the Julian calendar of Julius Caesar was reformed by Pope Gregory XIII in 1582

explanation.surface: A Roman emperor's schedule revised by a pontiff.
explanation.walkthrough: Caesar's 'timetable' is the Julian calendar; Pope Gregory's reform gave the Gregorian calendar, called this in Britain after 1752.
explanation.definitionFit: Dates reckoned by the Gregorian calendar are given this label, as against Old Style Julian dates.

clue.text: Be obstructive to one on a horse

parts.note: to stall is to play for time and obstruct
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone gets in the way of a rider.
explanation.definitionFit: An uncastrated male horse kept for breeding is called this.

clue.text: Stimulated to use a rod in the circumstances

indicators.note: in the circumstances suggests the preceding letters are arranged as conditions dictate, an anagram signal

explanation.surface: Someone provoked into using a stick given what happened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the circumstances' rearranges USE A ROD.
explanation.definitionFit: Being excited or stirred into action is to be roused.

parts.note: a kitchen aid shaped like a narrow-waisted sand glass, which sounds like a shapely kitchen maid

explanation.surface: A curvaceous kitchen helper.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'assistant' seems to be a shapely maid, but it is the little sand glass used to time boiling.
explanation.definitionFit: The small sand glass used to time boiling has the narrow-waisted shape of an hourglass.

indicators.note: order tells us to put the letters into a new arrangement

parts.note: another is read as 'an other', giving AN

explanation.surface: A drunken partygoer placed yet another order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' is split as 'an other', so its tail 'other' joins 'order' as the signal to rearrange; a Maenad is a frenzied female follower of Bacchus.
explanation.definitionFit: A frenzied female follower of Bacchus, god of wine, is one of the classical reveller-women.

explanation.surface: Dieters shun the greasy stuff candles are made of.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two nouns it is candle wax as a fat; read as a verb phrase, to 'wax' is to grow, so it is putting on weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Candle tallow is a kind of grease, and to grow plump is something dieters avoid.

clue.text: Peaked cap, made by Cheshire tailor?

parts.note: Cheshire is a well-known English cheese
a cutter is a tailor who cuts the cloth

explanation.surface: A peaked cap made by a tailor from the county of Cheshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheshire is an English county and its cheese; the cap is named for a wire for slicing cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a flat cap with a large peak, named after the shape of a wedge-slicing tool.

indicators.note: breaking up means the word before it is broken apart and its letters reassembled

explanation.surface: A couple announcing their split over who keeps the pottery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking up' rearranges WERE.
explanation.definitionFit: A water jug or pitcher is a kind of container.

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O
a lid is a cap or cover

explanation.surface: A round hat worn to display seniority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rank' looks like a military grade; it is the adjective for foul-smelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Olid is an old word for foul-smelling or foetid, which is rank in its smell sense.

parts.note: to stick is to stay or keep, as in 'stick to the path'
sake is Japanese rice wine, sometimes called rice beer

explanation.surface: A note telling someone to keep drinking only Japanese rice beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A memento kept for its associations serves as a token of remembrance.

explanation.surface: Someone tidying up a pile of bandages.
explanation.walkthrough: Soldiers dress their ranks by aligning them in straight lines, and a wound dressing is the material covering it.
explanation.definitionFit: Aligning troops in a straight line is called this on the parade ground, and gauze or lint on a wound is likewise named.
